minutes.headline: Task force plans to make the mini-split project the main fall Green Communities grant request; department submittals are due August 15.
minutes.summary: The Green Community task force approved the June 3 minutes and discussed the next grant round. Town departments have not responded, so a public comment appeal to the select board was planned, and the school mini-split project would be combined with its first phase as a single grant project. Members also heard a social media update and street light bill savings, discussed a possible Lunenburg Ledger article, and heard an unconfirmed report that the state may threaten Green Communities money over MBTA compliance. The next meeting stays August 5th.

what_happened.line: The task force plans to make the school mini-split project the main request in the fall Green Communities grant round, combined with its first phase as one project.
Town departments have not responded to the call for grant projects, so the chair planned to appeal to the select board during public comment.
Members compared a June street light bill with earlier bills to show savings from the new lights, and agreed to publish the bills as a table.
Members heard an unconfirmed report that the state may threaten Green Communities money over MBTA compliance; the discussion ended with no resolution.
The task force agreed to pursue a Lunenburg Ledger article on the street lights, with a short note on the fall grant round.

why_it_matters: The mini-split project is a school building upgrade, and combining it with its first phase is meant to show the town's own prior investment so that grant money only supplements completion.
Street light savings stay in their line item until year end, then can fund underfunded lines or roll to free cash, so the savings shape what is left for other town costs.
Green Communities grants depend on town departments submitting projects, and the state-aid risk raised at the meeting was not confirmed in the minutes.
